name: Daily Mail cryptic crossword, book 2 No 33

book.title: Daily Mail New Cryptic Crosswords, volume 2

clue.text: Top dodge for quick three

blocks.note: a top hat, or simply a hat worn on top
a dodge is a crafty ruse

explanation.surface: Someone looking for a fast way to win at something in three moves.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a hat trick is three wickets from three successive balls, hence three in quick order.
explanation.definitionFit: A hat trick is three successes achieved in rapid succession, typically goals or wickets.

clue.text: Not being seen to give punishment

definitions.note: the noun is given a hiding

blocks.note: first meaning: keeping out of sight
second meaning: a beating, as in to give someone a good one

explanation.surface: Someone lying low to avoid having to discipline anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means concealment, and colloquially also a thrashing or severe beating.

clue.text: Time for drinks, they're told

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
ales are beers

explanation.surface: Drinkers are informed it is time to go to the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Stories are things recounted, so they're told is a cryptic description of narratives.

clue.text: Make nonsense of a list of duties

blocks.note: rot is rubbish or nonsense
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone scrambling a schedule of chores.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests messing up the schedule, but nonsense simply provides a short word.
explanation.definitionFit: A rota is a schedule saying who takes their turn at which tasks.

clue.text: Ruin act that maybe ends the show

indicators.note: maybe signals the preceding words in some other possible order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A disastrous performance that might close a production early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruin' looks like the instruction but it is part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The curtain falls at a theatre performance's finish, so it brings the play to a close.

clue.text: About to do something at American plant

blocks.note: c. is short for circa, Latin for about
to act is to do something
abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: Someone getting busy at a factory belonging to an American firm.
explanation.definitionFit: The cactus is a spiny succulent native to the Americas, a type of desert vegetation.

clue.text: Fuss getting sailors to deck

blocks.note: ado is fuss, as in much ado
the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Commotion as sailors head up onto the ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: Deck sounds nautical with the sailors around, but it is the verb meaning decorate.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck is to decorate, as in deck the halls, the same as ornament.

clue.text: Latest in a move to provoke

indicators.note: a move shifts things about, so the letters are put in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The newest step in a campaign designed to stir someone up.
explanation.definitionFit: To tantalise is to tease or torment by showing something that is withheld, so to provoke.

clue.text: Duck transport rise and get together

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means reading the word from bottom to top

blocks.note: a bus is public transport
to merge is to combine

explanation.surface: Ducks rising from water and gathering, or an amphibious vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: Duck is the verb meaning plunge under water, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck someone is to push them under water, which is to immerse or plunge them.

clue.text: Slack politician having got a cover back

indicators.note: going back means these letters are read from the end towards the start

blocks.note: a lid is a cover
a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A lazy politician has been given cover for his failings.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed piece comes first in the answer although the politician is named first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Slack and dilatory both describe someone slow, tardy and inclined to delay work.

clue.text: Associate with superior person at a hot spot

blocks.note: a hob is the heated cooking surface on a stove
nob is British slang for a toff or upper-class person

explanation.surface: Mixing socially with a posh person at some fashionable venue.
explanation.walkthrough: The hob comes before the nob in the answer even though it is named second.
explanation.definitionFit: To hobnob is to mix socially, especially with people of higher standing.

clue.text: Favourites on the way up making progress

indicators.note: in a down entry going up means reading the word from bottom to top

blocks.note: teachers' pets are favourites

explanation.surface: Favoured contenders rising in the rankings.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is a stage of advance, so taking one is a move forward.

clue.text: It's part of one statutory duty to make a home

indicators.note: part of tells us the answer is a run of letters lying inside the following words

blocks.note: letters running across the end of one word and start of the next

explanation.surface: Providing housing is part of a legal obligation.
explanation.walkthrough: The book prints one's, but the letters needed run from one straight into statutory, so the apostrophe and s are a misreading.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest is a bird's home, and by extension any snug dwelling.

clue.text: Some harness for return transport in bad weather

indicators.note: a return journey goes back the way it came, so the word for the transport runs backwards

blocks.note: a tram is a form of public transport
taken as written
a gale is a strong wind

explanation.surface: Taking a trip home in stormy conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is in front; 'Some harness' means one kind of harness.
explanation.definitionFit: A martingale is a strap in a horse's tack that stops it raising its head too high.

clue.text: On your head be it!

blocks.note: surface reading: the warning that the blame will fall on you
setter's reading: the thing that literally sits on top of one's scalp

explanation.walkthrough: The stock phrase about accepting responsibility is read literally as a description.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair is what grows on top of everyone's scalp, literally located up there.

clue.text: Gives instruction for shooting when seeing one that moves

blocks.note: a coach trains people by instructing them
to pot is to shoot game, as in a pot shot

explanation.surface: A firearms instructor teaching people to hit a moving target.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'one that moves' sounds like a deer or clay, but it is a railway engine being spotted.
explanation.definitionFit: Trainspotting is the hobby of watching railway locomotives and noting their numbers.

clue.text: What a child may love to carry after last night whirl

indicators.note: the final letter of the following word is taken

blocks.note: the end of the word
an eddy is a swirl of water
to bear is to carry

explanation.surface: A child twirling around after the late night out.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuddly toy that children adore and often take to bed is the classic beloved comforter.

clue.text: Ready for some court activity

blocks.note: first meaning: prepared
second meaning: a stage of a tennis match made of games

explanation.surface: Prepared for a legal hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: Court suggests law, but it is a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means prepared, and in tennis a set is a group of games forming part of a match.

clue.text: Catch a bit of a rise

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means reading the word from bottom to top

blocks.note: a part is a bit

explanation.surface: Seizing a share of a pay increase.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonyms as verbs: to capture an animal or person by snaring them in a device or ambush.

clue.text: Search one goes on to seek an answer

blocks.note: a quest is a search
the Roman numeral for one
on means continuing, as in carry on

explanation.surface: A searcher keeps going in pursuit of a solution.
explanation.definitionFit: To question is to ask, which means trying to get a reply from someone.

clue.text: Set no store by low valuation

blocks.note: first meaning: to rate something too cheaply, as a verb
second meaning: a figure put on something that is too small, as a noun

explanation.surface: Not valuing something much, and pricing it cheaply.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for rating too lowly and a noun for a guess that falls short.

clue.text: Needled when bridge partners embrace opponents

indicators.note: embracing means holding around, so one pair goes round the other

blocks.note: South and North sit opposite each other as a partnership in bridge
East and West are the opposing partnership

explanation.surface: Players got irritated when their partners went over to the other side.
explanation.walkthrough: Needled looks like annoyed, but it means stitched with a needle.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sewn has been worked with needle and thread, so it has been needled.

clue.text: Raise difficulty over some line taken by a country person

indicators.note: a difficulty is trouble, so the preceding word is put into disorder
some means only part of the following word is used

blocks.note: the letters of this word rearranged
the opening pair of the word

explanation.surface: Someone making problems over a political line adopted by a country.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry over means placed above, so the rearranged letters come first.
explanation.definitionFit: An Israeli is a citizen of Israel, a person from that nation.

clue.text: Don't agree to a thing!

blocks.note: first meaning: protest, as a verb
second meaning: an item, as a noun

explanation.surface: An exclamation refusing to consent to anything at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Stressed one way it means protest; stressed the other it is a physical item.

clue.text: Make a pronouncement to get something started

blocks.note: first meaning: literally utter the term
second meaning: the idiom for giving the go-ahead

explanation.surface: An official announcement launching a project.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means give the signal and something will happen at once; literally it means utter a term.

clue.text: Greeting suffering at the official opening

indicators.note: an opening is the start, so only the first letter of official is used

blocks.note: hell is torment
only the start of this word is kept

explanation.surface: A miserable welcome given at a formal launch ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Hello is the standard salutation used when meeting someone.

clue.text: Don't start to go up a tree to get a branch

indicators.note: telling the phrase not to start means its opening letter is dropped

blocks.note: to climb is to go up

explanation.surface: Advice to a child not to climb a tree to reach a bough.
explanation.definitionFit: A limb is a large bough of a tree as well as an arm or leg.

clue.text: One has to tear around getting hot

indicators.note: around suggests the word is turned about into some other order

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
the letters of this word rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who has to rush about and gets sweaty.
explanation.walkthrough: Hot here is hot under the collar, not warm.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot-tempered or hot under the collar means angry, the same as furious.

clue.text: Last character to appear in third-rate metal

blocks.note: the final letter of the alphabet
taken as written
a C grade is third after A and B

explanation.surface: A villain finally turning up in a poor-quality heavy metal act.
explanation.definitionFit: Zinc is a bluish-white metallic chemical element used in galvanising.

clue.text: Models that embarrass ladies

indicators.note: to embarrass is to throw into confusion, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fashion models whose looks make other women feel awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideals are perfect examples to imitate, which is what models are in this sense.

clue.text: Tied lace so as to look elegant

indicators.note: the letters are rearranged so that they take on a new appearance

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fastening a lacy garment to appear stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Delicate means fine and dainty, close to graceful or refined in appearance.

clue.text: Point and pointer circumscribed

blocks.note: north is a compass point
an arrow points the way

explanation.surface: A sign and its arrow, read as a narrow little phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Something circumscribed is tightly limited in scope, which is what narrow means.

clue.text: Not telling small girl what might be secret

indicators.note: what might be suggests the following word in some other possible form

blocks.note: Di is a short form of the girl's name Diana
the letters of this word rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl who keeps quiet about something hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: A discreet person is careful to keep quiet and avoid revealing confidences.
